name: KY-002 vibration switch
identification: Small black PCB with 3 angled header pins at one end and a black upright cylinder about as tall as the board is wide. The KY-017 has a similar black cylinder lying flat; the KY-012 and KY-006 buzzers are much wider.

middle.say: middle pin, the one between S and minus

confirmations.question: Look at the 3 pins of the vibration switch. Is one marked S and one marked with a minus, with the third pin between them?
confirmations.reason: The pin order differs between modules. The wiring plan is only valid if S and minus are the outer pins and the supply pin is the one in the middle.

facts.statement: The module has three pins: signal (printed S), supply (+V, the middle pin) and ground (printed -). The vendor's drawing shows them in the order S, supply, -. Go by the printed markings.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-002, pin drawing (vendor documentation for the Joy-IT module; clones may differ)

facts.statement: The vendor's technical data gives an operating voltage of 3.3 V to 5 V.

A spring inside closes a contact on a shock. The vendor's example reports a vibration while the signal is LOW. Powered from 3.3 V the signal cannot rise above 3.3 V. The vendor's Arduino example switches on the board's internal pull-up resistor for this pin; LearnLens sketches do not, so whether the signal is stable without it is not confirmed.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-002, description and code example
